Zimbabwe Metals & Mining Sector Posts Stable Growth Amid Favorable Market Conditions

Zimbabwe’s metals and mining industry reported steady growth in its latest quarterly results, buoyed by robust international demand and supportive government policies. According to data released by the Zimbabwe Chamber of Mines, overall mineral output rose 4.6% for the quarter ending March 2024, compared to the same period last year.

Nickel and platinum group metals (PGMs) led sector gains, with output climbing 7% and 6.2% respectively. ZimMetals, one of the country’s leading producers, attributed the uptick to improved efficiencies at its Bindura operations. “Our investments in modern processing technology are starting to bear fruit,” said ZimMetals CEO, Tendai Moyo. “We’ve managed to optimize recovery rates while maintaining a strong safety record.”

Gold production also registered a modest 3.1% increase, reaching 7.8 tonnes for the quarter. Analysts note that favorable global prices and a stable local currency contributed to the sector’s performance. “The international metals market remains supportive, and Zimbabwean producers are capitalizing on this window,” said Tapiwa Ncube, an analyst at Harare-based consultancy Resource Insight.

The Zimbabwe Mining Federation highlighted ongoing engagement with government authorities to streamline export procedures, which industry leaders say will further enhance sector competitiveness. “Our focus is on maintaining consistency in output and compliance with environmental standards,” said Federation president Farai Chikafu.

While challenges such as power supply constraints and logistics remain, industry stakeholders expressed optimism for continued growth. The Chamber of Mines projects total mineral export earnings could surpass $4.2 billion this year if current trends persist.
